title: One noisy cellular automaton with an uncomputable noise diagram
description: Can varying only the noise rate of one cellular automaton encode halting? We construct one computably specified finite-alphabet, finite-range automaton on Z^4 with computable disjoint rational open rate windows. Throughout the nth window, uniform whole-symbol replacement is ergodic exactly when a fixed universal machine halts on n. Halting gives exponential coalescence simultaneously over all initial configurations and attraction from every initial law; nonhalting gives two laws invariant under every spatial translation. Planar rulers and computation boards select the input; three transverse quorum boxes, marked-parent density and interval sensors control errors. The space-time construction gives one fixed translation-invariant finite-range {0,1}-energy interaction on Z^5 with computable rational inverse-temperature windows: halting is equivalent to uniqueness among all Gibbs measures and also gives exponential weak spatial mixing in arbitrary volumes. The earlier Z^6 and Z^7 constructions, their extremal and field-response results, and the Lean verification of Theorem A and its stated corollaries are retained. The Z^4 theorem and Z^5 corollary are not formalized.
notes: Preprint. It has not been peer reviewed. Version 1.3.0 updates version 1.2.0 (10.5281/zenodo.24174445). New Section 10: Theorem C, one fixed finite-alphabet finite-range automaton on Z^4 with computable rational rate windows on which it is ergodic exactly when a universal machine halts, with exponential all-input coalescence on halting windows; and Corollary D, one fixed {0,1}-energy interaction on Z^5 whose uniqueness among all Gibbs measures on computable windows is equivalent to halting. The Z^4 parameters are certified by two independent exact-arithmetic programs (verification/z4-scale/).
